extracted.intended_audience: general readers, fans and researchers of television/comedy
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedia-style article summarizing the American adult puppet sketch-comedy series Wonder Showzen: production details, genres, episode guides, recurring segments, broadcast history and reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed genres in the infobox: Adult puppeteering; Sketch comedy; Black comedy; Horror comedy; Surreal humour; Parody; Political satire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to categorize the show and set audience expectations; appears verbatim in the article's infobox as the show's genre labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parody of children's educational shows (format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Described as a children's television series for kids; the show's format is a parody of educational PBS Kids shows such as Sesame Street and The Electric Company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The parody format includes use of stock footage, puppetry, and clips of children being interviewed — structural and stylistic devices that define the show's approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satirical targets and tone
rubrics_metrics.description: The series satirizes politics, religion, war, violence, sex, racism and culture with comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article emphasizes that in addition to general controversial comedy, the series intentionally attacks a wide range of sensitive topics — framing its tone as subversive and controversial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurring segment: Beat Kids
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the children, most often Trevor, leads a journalistic segment with mostly offensive, humorous questions, ridiculing interviewees at a given venue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears in almost every episode; functions as a recurring device to elicit child-led, provocative interviews and humor based on discomfort/insult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurring segment: Funny/Not Funny
rubrics_metrics.description: A series of clips, often depicting violent or macabre images, airs with a chorus of children saying either 'funny' or 'not funny'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses children’s reactions to juxtapose innocence and dark imagery; example of the show's confrontational comedic techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurring segment: Clarence's Movies / Clarence interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarence the puppet interviews people on the street on a common theme, usually antagonistically or obnoxiously, often reciprocated by violence or threats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recurring confrontational vox-pop segment that frequently escalates to extreme responses; exemplifies the show's shock-humor style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurring segment: Q&A
rubrics_metrics.description: A series of children each answer a single question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple format used repeatedly throughout episodes to produce unexpected, often darkly comic answers from children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurring segment: So Now You Know (parody PSA)
rubrics_metrics.description: A parody of 'The More You Know', where kids say questions and a computer shows their answers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parodic PSA-style segment that satirizes educational public-service formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurring segment: Mr. Body
rubrics_metrics.description: A cartoon segment that parodies the Slim Goodbody character from Captain Kangaroo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Animation-based parody of children's educational health segments; example of interstitial cartoons used to mimic and subvert familiar children’s TV tropes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurring segment: D.O.G.O.B.G.Y.N (cartoon)
rubrics_metrics.description: A cartoon chronicling a dog with the ability to aid in childbirth; title references obstetrics and gynecology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example of the show's absurd and adult-oriented cartoon inserts that parody medical/educational programming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode structure and running time
rubrics_metrics.description: Episodes are sketch-based, containing many short sketches and recurring segments; running time is 21–22 minutes per episode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard half-hour (with commercials) sketch-comedy format; each episode aggregates many short bits (Q&A, cartoons, Breaking News, etc.) to form a theme-based program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of child interviewees and staged innocence
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequent use of clips of children being interviewed and children participating in segments (e.g., Beat Kids, Q&A, Funny/Not Funny).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The contrast between children's apparent innocence and the adult/controversial subject matter is a central comedic device; producers exploit that juxtaposition for shock and satire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production and technical elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Production details: produced by PFFR Productions and USA Cable Entertainment; camera setup multi-camera; animation services by Raw Power (first episode) and Augenblick Studios (rest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These concrete production choices (production company, multi-camera setup, choice of animators) shape the show's aesthetic and logistical constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guest cameos and celebrity appearances
rubrics_metrics.description: Series features many cameos (e.g., Flavor Flav, Dick Gregory, Amy Sedaris, David Cross, Amy Poehler, Zach Galifianakis), sometimes with segments cut from broadcast but included on DVD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of known comedic personalities both enhances reach and supplies additional comedic styles; noted instances include unaired material released on home video.

rubrics_metrics.name: Home-release features and fan engagement (animation contest)
rubrics_metrics.description: Season-one DVD included extras; season-two DVD included an easter egg that featured an animation contest whose grand prize was the winner's animation appearing on 'the next DVD'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DVD bonus features and contests used to engage fans and generate extra content; producers later indicated a third season was unlikely despite the contest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadcast variations and censorship
rubrics_metrics.description: International broadcast differences: in Turkey, it aired on Euro D with graphic scenes cut; streaming on Paramount+ omits episodes 'History' and 'Time'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Versions and availability can vary by territory/platform; content edits and omitted episodes are part of the show's distribution reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical reception and influence
rubrics_metrics.description: The show received critical praise (first season holds 100% on Rotten Tomatoes) and endorsements from creators/comics (e.g., Matt Groening, Eric André).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited praise frames the show's cultural impact and influence on later surreal/subversive comedy (Eric André cites it as an influence on his show).
